jobs.title: Oenologist
jobs.description:
Job Profiles
Oenologist
Part scientist, technician, legal expert, and manager, the Oenologist is a specialist in wine and the wine market. They are involved at every stage of wine production, from harvest to bottling, and provide support to both winegrowers and commercial players in the industry.
Main Responsibilities
Oenologist plays a key role in the wine and spirits industry:
- Ensure Wine Quality: They select grape varieties and analyze the soil, advise on vine treatment and harvest dates, supervise winemaking and distillation, define preservation processes, and handle blending and bottling.
- Evaluate and Control: They design analytical methods and perform chemical and organoleptic tests to correct any defects.
- Tasting Professional: With a highly developed sense of taste and smell, they evaluate wines, advise producers, and play a commercial role with clients.
- Contribute to Commercial Strategy: They negotiate contracts, promote specific vintages, and develop sales plans.
- Manage: They lead technical teams and collaborate with winegrowers, distributors, and major retailers.
Required Skills
A sharp scientific profile and multidisciplinary skills are essential:
- Biology of vines, biochemistry, chemical, and microbiological analyses.
- In-depth knowledge of winemaking, preservation, and blending methods.
- Mastery of tasting techniques and cellar-based corrections.
- A grasp of wine law and production regulations.
- Marketing, communication, and commercial strategy applied to wine.
- Project management and team leadership.
Essential Soft Skills
The Oenologist must also possess key personal qualities:
- Good physical health to maintain olfactory and gustatory abilities.
- The ability to work alone or as part of a team.
- Listening skills, communication, and a pedagogical approach.
- A sense of responsibility and composure.
- Motivation, perseverance, and a passion for wine.
- Analytical and focused mindset.
- Vigilance and scientific rigor.
Career Opportunities and Employers
An Oenologist can work in various environments:
- Wineries and cooperative cellars (consulting, supervision, quality control).
- Major retail chains (purchasing and selecting wines).
- Manufacturers of winemaking equipment (technical expertise).
- High-end restaurants and hotels (as a sommelier or wine advisor).
- Freelance: as a consultant or oenology advisor.
Difference Between a Sommelier and an Oenologist
- Oenologist: Is involved throughout the entire wine production process (scientific, technical, and strategic).
- Sommelier: Works after production, manages a restaurant's wine cellar, selects wines, and suggests food-and-wine pairings.
Note: A sommelier works closely with the chef to create pairings that enhance both the dishes and the beverages.
Education and Degrees
- The National Oenologist Diploma (DNO) , a Bac +5 degree (Master's level), is mandatory to practice.
- The MBA in Wine & Spirits Management (Vatel Bordeaux) is a specialized training in wine business management, accessible in the second year of an MBA in hospitality, even without prior wine-related prerequisites.
Salary
- Entry-level: Around €2,000 gross per month.
- Experienced: Between €2,500 and €5,000 gross per month.
Note: The salary varies significantly depending on experience, the wine region, and employment status (employee, freelancer, consultant).
Career Progression
With experience, an oenologist can advance to:
- Wine and spirits trader.
- Buyer for a major retail chain.
- Chef de rang or sommelier in a fine-dining restaurant.
- Event project manager (trade shows, tastings, international fairs).
- Wine merchant or independent consultant.
Success Stories of Vatel Graduates
In France and internationally, the 50,000 Vatel alumni build exemplary, innovative, and exciting careers every day. They work in diverse sectors such as luxury hospitality, gourmet restaurants, event management, hotel marketing, luxury management, oenology, cruises, international tourism, and the wine & spirits industry.

jobs.title: Ecolodge Director
jobs.description:
Job Profiles
Ecolodge Director
The role of Ecolodge Director allows you to play a key part in ecotourism. Leading an environmentally responsible establishment, you ensure a balance between economic profitability, biodiversity conservation, and the involvement of local communities.
Job Description: Ecolodge Director
- Recruiting and training teams, prioritizing the local population, in order to reinforce sustainable and cultural development.
- Administrative, budgetary, and logistical monitoring: Ensuring operational management, promoting cultural diversity, and limiting negative environmental effects.
- Communication and awareness: Promoting the establishment, highlighting the transparency of ecological practices, and educating travelers on the protection of flora and fauna.
Skills and Personal Qualities
Technical Skills
- In-depth knowledge of sustainable development (eco-friendly materials, understanding of local traditions, administrative procedures).
- Mastery of environmental standards and certifications (e.g., Green Globe label¹).
- Aptitude in communication and marketing to promote the offering and educate clients.
- Skills in hotel management and general management to oversee an establishment.
Human Qualities
- Ecological and ethical sensitivity.
- Leadership and the ability to unite a multicultural team.
- Organization, rigor, and analytical mindset.
- Cultural openness and diplomacy.
- Entrepreneurial spirit and capacity for innovation.
Education and Qualifications
- Training in hospitality and catering ( Bachelor's in International Hospitality , BTS [Higher Technician Certificate], Professional Licenses).
- MBA in International Hospitality to acquire managerial and strategic expertise in responsible tourism.
Prior experience in the hotel industry or in the management of tourism structures is highly recommended .
Working Conditions
- Environment in direct connection with nature and local populations .
- Flexible hours , often intense during high season.
- High responsibility in ecological, economic, and social management .
Salary
- Average salary: €2,500 to €4,000 gross per month, depending on the size, location, and management style (independent or group).
Career Progression
After a few years, the Ecolodge Director can advance to:
- Directing a larger establishment or one belonging to an ecotourism chain.
- Progressing to a general director position in the sustainable hospitality sector.
- Creating or developing their own ecotourism project.
Success Stories of Vatel Graduates
In France and internationally, the 50,000 Vatel alumni build exemplary, innovative, and exciting careers every day. They work in diverse sectors such as luxury hospitality, gourmet restaurants, event management, hotel marketing, luxury management, oenology, cruises, international tourism, and the wine & spirits industry.

jobs.title: Sports Event Project Manager
jobs.description:
Job Profiles
Sports Event Project Manager
The Sports Event Project Manager plays a strategic role in designing, organizing, and ensuring the success of sports events. Their goal is to plan and oversee all operations, deliver an optimal experience for participants, clients, and partners, while respecting budgets and achieving event objectives.
Responsibilities
The Sports Event Project Manager coordinates all stages of a sports event and acts as the liaison between internal teams, partners, and external service providers. Key responsibilities include:
- Event planning and design: define the concept, program, objectives, and budget of the event.
- Team and vendor coordination: manage logistics, communications, ticketing, and partner teams, and supervise service providers (catering, security, audiovisual).
- Operational management: organize and monitor installations, on-site logistics, participant flows, and safety.
- Financial and strategic oversight: ensure budget compliance, optimize costs, and analyze the event’s profitability and impact.
- Communication and promotion: collaborate with marketing and PR to promote the event and enhance brand visibility.
- Evaluation and improvement: gather feedback from participants, partners, and sponsors, and suggest improvements for future editions.
Required Skills
To succeed in this role, a Sports Event Project Manager must combine organizational, interpersonal, and strategic skills:
- Project management and organization: plan, coordinate, and supervise complex teams and operations.
- Communication and client relations: effectively interact with clients, partners, and sponsors.
- Financial skills: manage budgets, analyze costs, and maximize event profitability.
- Digital proficiency: event management software, office tools, and ticketing platforms.
- Soft skills: rigor, creativity, initiative, stress management, and strategic thinking.
- Foreign languages: English is essential for international events; a second language is a plus.
Education and Training
The role typically requires a Bachelor’s or MBA Vatel in Hospitality and tourism: programs focusing on customer service, VIP hospitality, and event organization.
Project management and leadership: specialization in team management and event coordination.
Previous experience in event planning, project management, or sports-related projects is highly valued.
Salary
The salary of a Sports Event Project Manager varies depending on the size and profile of the event or organization:
- Entry-level: €2,500 – €3,500 gross per month
- Mid-level: €3,500 – €5,500 gross per month
- Senior / international events: up to €7,000 gross per month, including bonuses and incentives
Career Progression
After several years in this role, a Sports Event Project Manager can advance to:
- Event Production Director
- Head of Sports Events for an organization or club
- Consultant in event management or sports marketing
- Founder and manager of their own event management agency

In France and internationally, the 50,000 Vatel alumni build exemplary, innovative, and exciting careers every day. They work in diverse sectors such as luxury hospitality, gourmet restaurants, event management, hotel marketing, luxury management, oenology, cruises, international tourism, and the wine & spirits industry.

jobs.description:
Job Profiles
Senior Living Residence Director
The Senior Living Residence Director supervises all residence operations and coordinates between internal teams, residents’ families, and external partners.
The Senior Living Residence Director supervises all residence operations and coordinates between internal teams, residents’ families, and external partners. Their key missions include:
- Operational and organizational management : Oversee the day-to-day operations of the residence (accommodation, catering, healthcare, activities, maintenance) and ensure a safe and comfortable environment for residents.
- Team management : Recruit, train, and supervise staff (caregivers, activity coordinators, hospitality and administrative teams), foster a positive work environment, and drive team performance.
- Financial and strategic management : Prepare and monitor the budget, optimize resources, track performance indicators, and propose continuous improvement strategies.
- Resident and family relations : Ensure resident well-being, address their needs, and maintain regular, transparent communication with families.
- Regulatory compliance and quality : Guarantee compliance with safety, hygiene, and social/healthcare regulations.
- Reporting to senior management : Present financial and operational results, monitor satisfaction indicators, and recommend strategies for residence development.
Key Skills
To succeed in this role, the Senior Living Residence Director must combine managerial, organizational, and interpersonal skills:
- Leadership and coordination : Ability to lead multidisciplinary teams and foster cohesion.
- Financial and administrative management : Strong command of budgeting and resource optimization.
- Quality of life and interpersonal skills : Active listening, empathy, and the ability to meet residents’ and families’ needs.
- Knowledge of the senior care sector : Familiarity with regulations, safety standards, and care practices.
- Soft skills : Rigor, organizational sense, strategic vision, strong communication, and leadership abilities.
Education and Qualifications
This role typically requires a Bachelor or MBA degree :
- Business administration or organizational management.
- Management of healthcare or social service facilities.
Salary
The salary of a Senior Living Residence Director varies depending on the size of the facility and experience:
- Entry level : €3,500 – €4,500 gross per month
- Experienced profile : €5,000 – €7,000 gross per month
- Senior / large groups : up to €9,000 gross per month, including bonuses and benefits
Career Development Opportunities
After several years in this role, the Senior Living Residence Director can move into positions such as:
- Regional Director or Director of multiple senior living facilities
- General Manager of a healthcare or senior care group
- Consultant in senior housing management or expert in healthcare strategy
- Entrepreneur in senior living facilities or advisory services

jobs.title: Restaurant Manager
jobs.description:
Job Profiles
Restaurant Manager
Are you passionate about hospitality and catering, and a born manager?
The profession of Restaurant Manager is for you. A true pillar of the establishment, he/she supervises all activities and ensure the overall performance of the restaurant, whether human, technical, financial, or administrative.
Main Duties
The Restaurant Manager acts as a true business leader. Their main duties include:
Human Resources Management: Recruitment, training, team supervision, scheduling, and task distribution.
Daily Operations Planning: Inventory management, supplier follow-up, client reception supervision, and coordination with the kitchen.
Profitability and Client Satisfaction: Menu development, pricing, budget monitoring, results analysis, and implementation of marketing strategies to promote the establishment.
Hygiene and Food Safety: Compliance and communication of current standards, control of team practices.
Team Management: Creating a positive work environment, motivating, and supporting staff.
Adaptation to Trends: Monitoring developments in the restaurant market (products, competition, client expectations).
Skills and Personal Qualities
Technical Skills
- Excellent culinary culture and knowledge of the hotel and restaurant sector.
- Skills in business management and financial steering.
- Mastery of digital tools and hospitality software.
- Strong sense of management and customer relations.
- Commercial and marketing capabilities.
Human Qualities
- Excellent communication and active listening.
- Empathy and sense of responsibility.
- Flexibility and adaptability.
- Organization and rigor.
- Ability to anticipate problems and quickly find solutions.
- Natural leadership and ability to motivate teams.
Training and Diplomas
- Possible access from a high school diploma (Bac) or Bac +2 (two years of higher education) with solid experience in catering.
- Specialized training: Bachelor in International Hospitality, BTS Hôtellerie-Restauration (Higher Technician Certificate in Hospitality-Catering), professional licenses in hotel management.
- MBA in International Hospitality: Allows for the acquisition of in-depth skills in management, finance, communication, and decision-making.
Working Conditions
- Demanding environment, requiring high availability (evenings, weekends, and holidays).
- High responsibilities for the overall performance of the restaurant.
- Constant contact with clients, teams, and external partners.
Salary
- Entry-level: Between €2,000 and €3,500 gross per month.
- Experienced / Senior: Up to €55,000 gross annually (depending on the size and prestige of the establishment).
Career Evolutions
- Possibilities for specialization (Commercial Director, Financial Director, General Manager).
- Taking charge of several establishments within a group or chain.
- Creation and management of one's own restaurant.

Are you passionate about hospitality and catering, and a born manager?
The profession of Restaurant Manager is for you. A true pillar of the establishment, he/she supervises all activities and ensure the overall performance of the restaurant, whether human, technical, financial, or administrative.
Main Duties
The Restaurant Manager acts as a true business leader. Their main duties include:
Human Resources Management: Recruitment, training, team supervision, scheduling, and task distribution.
Daily Operations Planning: Inventory management, supplier follow-up, client reception supervision, and coordination with the kitchen.
Profitability and Client Satisfaction: Menu development, pricing, budget monitoring, results analysis, and implementation of marketing strategies to promote the establishment.
Hygiene and Food Safety: Compliance and communication of current standards, control of team practices.
Team Management: Creating a positive work environment, motivating, and supporting staff.
Adaptation to Trends: Monitoring developments in the restaurant market (products, competition, client expectations).
Skills and Personal Qualities
Technical Skills
- Excellent culinary culture and knowledge of the hotel and restaurant sector.
- Skills in business management and financial steering.
- Mastery of digital tools and hospitality software.
- Strong sense of management and customer relations.
- Commercial and marketing capabilities.
Human Qualities
- Excellent communication and active listening.
- Empathy and sense of responsibility.
- Flexibility and adaptability.
- Organization and rigor.
- Ability to anticipate problems and quickly find solutions.
- Natural leadership and ability to motivate teams.
Training and Diplomas
- Possible access from a high school diploma (Bac) or Bac +2 (two years of higher education) with solid experience in catering.
- Specialized training: Bachelor in International Hospitality, BTS Hôtellerie-Restauration (Higher Technician Certificate in Hospitality-Catering), professional licenses in hotel management.
- MBA in International Hospitality: Allows for the acquisition of in-depth skills in management, finance, communication, and decision-making.
Working Conditions
- Demanding environment, requiring high availability (evenings, weekends, and holidays).
- High responsibilities for the overall performance of the restaurant.
- Constant contact with clients, teams, and external partners.
Salary
- Entry-level: Between €2,000 and €3,500 gross per month.

Career Evolutions
- Possibilities for specialization (Commercial Director, Financial Director, General Manager).
- Taking charge of several establishments within a group or chain.
- Creation and management of one's own restaurant.

jobs.title: Food and Beverage Director
jobs.description:
Job Profiles
Food and Beverage Director
The Food and Beverage Director, also known as F&B Manager, is a key executive in hotels, resorts, and high-end establishments. They coordinate and supervise all activities related to food and beverage services.
The Food and Beverage Director has a strategic and operational role:
- Supervise all food and beverage outlets (restaurants, bars, room service, banquets, catering, etc.).
- Guarantee service quality and customer satisfaction , ensuring compliance with the establishment's standards.
- Manage teams: Recruit, train, motivate, and evaluate front-of-house, bar, and sometimes kitchen staff.
- Optimize financial management: Control costs, negotiate with suppliers, monitor turnover and profitability.
- Implement commercial and marketing actions to develop business (promotions, partnerships, events).
- Comply with hygiene and food safety standards across all food and beverage areas.
Skills of a Food and Beverage Manager
To succeed in this highly responsible position, several skills are essential:
- Leadership and management: Ability to supervise and motivate large, multidisciplinary teams.
- Organization and management: Rigorous monitoring of inventory, budgets, and profitability.
- Excellent communication: Smooth relations with clients, suppliers, and management.
- Knowledge of F&B trends and new practices in gastronomy and mixology.
- Proficiency in foreign languages , especially English, essential in international hospitality.
- Commercial and marketing aptitudes to optimize the image and revenues of food and beverage services.
Training to Become a Food and Beverage Director
A Food & Beverage Manager position is generally obtained after several years of experience in catering and/or hospitality, often as a Chef de Rang, Maître d'hôtel, or Restaurant Manager.
The most suitable training programs include:
- BTS Hôtellerie-Restauration (Higher Technician Certificate in Hospitality-Catering) with a management option;
- Bachelor's degree in Hotel Management;
- Specialized MBA in Hospitality, Catering, and Tourism;
- Further training in management, hospitality management, or marketing.
Salary of a Food and Beverage Director
Remuneration varies according to the size of the establishment and the level of responsibility:
- Entry-level: Between €3,000 and €3,500 gross per month;
- Experienced: Between €4,500 and €6,000 gross per month;
- In international luxury hospitality: Salary can exceed €8,000 gross per month, along with benefits (accommodation, bonuses).
Possible Career Evolutions
After several years of experience, a Food & Beverage Manager can progress to:
- Hotel Director or General Manager of a resort;
- Director of Operations in a hotel chain;
- Catering or Hotel Management Consultant ;
- Creator or Manager of their own establishment (restaurant, hotel, F&B concept).
Success Stories of Vatel Graduates
In France and internationally, the 50,000 Vatel alumni build exemplary, innovative, and exciting careers every day. They work in diverse sectors such as luxury hospitality, gourmet restaurants, event management, hotel marketing, luxury management, oenology, cruises, international tourism, and the wine & spirits industry.

- Guarantee service quality and customer satisfaction , ensuring compliance with the establishment's standards.
- Manage teams: Recruit, train, motivate, and evaluate front-of-house, bar, and sometimes kitchen staff.
- Optimize financial management: Control costs, negotiate with suppliers, monitor turnover and profitability.
- Implement commercial and marketing actions to develop business (promotions, partnerships, events).
- Comply with hygiene and food safety standards across all food and beverage areas.
Skills of a Food and Beverage Manager
To succeed in this highly responsible position, several skills are essential:
- Leadership and management: Ability to supervise and motivate large, multidisciplinary teams.
- Organization and management: Rigorous monitoring of inventory, budgets, and profitability.
- Excellent communication: Smooth relations with clients, suppliers, and management.
- Knowledge of F&B trends and new practices in gastronomy and mixology.
- Proficiency in foreign languages , especially English, essential in international hospitality.
- Commercial and marketing aptitudes to optimize the image and revenues of food and beverage services.
Training to Become a Food and Beverage Director
A Food & Beverage Manager position is generally obtained after several years of experience in catering and/or hospitality, often as a Chef de Rang, Maître d'hôtel, or Restaurant Manager.
The most suitable training programs include:
- BTS Hôtellerie-Restauration (Higher Technician Certificate in Hospitality-Catering) with a management option;
- Bachelor's degree in Hotel Management;
- Specialized MBA in Hospitality, Catering, and Tourism;
- Further training in management, hospitality management, or marketing.
Salary of a Food and Beverage Director
Remuneration varies according to the size of the establishment and the level of responsibility:
- Entry-level: Between €3,000 and €3,500 gross per month;
- Experienced: Between €4,500 and €6,000 gross per month;
- In international luxury hospitality: Salary can exceed €8,000 gross per month, along with benefits (accommodation, bonuses).
Possible Career Evolutions
After several years of experience, a Food & Beverage Manager can progress to:
- Hotel Director or General Manager of a resort;
- Director of Operations in a hotel chain;
- Catering or Hotel Management Consultant ;
- Creator or Manager of their own establishment (restaurant, hotel, F&B concept).

jobs.title: Human Resources Manager in Hospitality
jobs.description:
Job Profiles
Human Resources Manager in Hospitality
The hotel and restaurant industry is one of the largest employers in France. In this demanding sector, the Human Resources Manager (HRM) plays a central role. Acting as a crucial link between management and the teams, they define and implement HR policy, manage recruitment and skills development, and ensure a good quality of life at work.
Key Responsibilities
The HR Manager is responsible for the effective management of human resources within a hotel or hotel group. Their duties are varied and include:
- Recruitment and Onboarding: Defining needs, selecting candidates, conducting interviews, and strengthening the employer brand.
- Talent Retention: Reducing employee turnover, establishing career paths, and ensuring internal communication and quality of life at work (QVT).
- Administrative Management: Overseeing contracts, managing schedules, and ensuring compliance with the Labor Code and the specific hourly constraints of the hospitality industry.
- Skills Development: Establishing a training plan, overseeing forward-looking employment and skills management (GPEC), and promoting internal career progression.
- Employee Relations: Facilitating dialogue with employee representatives, negotiating agreements, and ensuring legal compliance.
Required Skills
Technical Skills
- Mastery of social law and the Labor Code.
- Proficiency with HR tools (HRIS, job boards, social media).
- Administrative management and development of training plans.
- Recruitment and retention techniques.
Personal Qualities
- Excellent listening skills and a sense of confidentiality.
- Tact, diplomacy, and the ability to manage conflicts.
- Strong written and interpersonal skills.
- Organization, meticulousness, and collaborative leadership.
Education
To become an HR Manager in hospitality, several educational paths are possible:
- A Master's degree in Human Resources, Social Law, or Management.
- Business schools or Political Science Institutes (IEP) with an HR specialization.
- Specialized HR schools (after a Bachelor's degree).
- An MBA in Hospitality (e.g., from Vatel) to gain industry-specific expertise.
Note: Initial experience as an HR Assistant, Recruitment Officer, or Personnel Manager in a hotel setting is essential to access this position.
Salary
The gross annual salary for an HR Manager in hospitality ranges from €35,000 to €61,000, with an average of approximately €47,000. Compensation depends on the size of the establishment, the group, and the level of responsibility.
Career Progression
With experience, an HR Manager can advance to roles such as:
- Human Resources Director (HRD) within a large hotel group.
- Multi-site or Regional HR Manager.
- Specialized Consultant (recruitment, training, coaching).
Success Stories of Vatel Graduates
In France and internationally, the 50,000 Vatel alumni build exemplary, innovative, and exciting careers every day. They work in diverse sectors such as luxury hospitality, gourmet restaurants, event management, hotel marketing, luxury management, oenology, cruises, international tourism, and the wine & spirits industry.

jobs.description:
Job Profiles
Hotel Development Director / Tourism Real Estate
The Hotel Development Director plays a crucial role in expanding a hotel group's portfolio by identifying new opportunities and managing real estate projects from start to finish.
The Hotel Development Director plays a crucial role in expanding a hotel group's portfolio by identifying new opportunities and managing real estate projects from start to finish. They act as the central point for internal teams, investors, and external partners.
Main responsibilities include:
- Site Identification and Acquisition: Analyzing the market, selecting suitable land or buildings, evaluating economic potential, and negotiating acquisitions.
- Real Estate Project Development: Supervising the construction, renovation, or expansion of hotels and tourist resorts in collaboration with architects, engineers, and urban planners.
- Financial and Strategic Management: Establishing provisional budgets, calculating project profitability, tracking investments, and proposing optimization strategies.
- Team and Partner Coordination: Managing internal teams (project, legal, finance) and collaborating with investors, banks, local authorities, and consulting firms.
- Regulatory and Legal Monitoring: Ensuring all projects comply with local standards, urban planning laws, safety, and environmental regulations.
- Reporting to General Management: Presenting project progress, financial results, and recommendations for future acquisitions or developments.
Required Skills
To succeed in this role, a Hotel Development Director must combine technical, financial, and managerial skills:
- Real Estate and Urban Planning Knowledge: Mastery of the technical aspects of construction, layout, and regulations.
- Financial Analysis and Project Management: The ability to calculate profitability, develop business plans, and manage a project from start to finish.
- Management and Coordination: The ability to lead multidisciplinary teams and work with various partners.
- Commercial and Negotiation Skills: The aptitude to convince investors, banks, and strategic partners.
- Foreign Language Proficiency: English is essential, and a second language is a plus in an international context.
- Soft Skills: Thoroughness, organizational skills, strategic thinking, communication abilities, and a long-term vision.
Training to Become a Hotel Development Director
The position generally requires a Master's degree (Bac+5 or equivalent) with a specialization in one of the following areas:
- Hospitality and Tourism: MBA in hotel management at Vatel or MBA in tourist real estate management.
- Real Estate and Urban Planning: Master's degree in real estate, finance, or real estate development.
- Project Management and Strategic Management.
Prior experience in hotel development, asset management, or hotel management is often essential.
Salary
The salary of a Hotel Development Director varies depending on the company's size, the type of project, and experience.
- Entry-level: €4,500 to €6,000 gross per month
- Experienced Profile: €8,000 to €12,000 gross per month
- Senior Director / Large International Groups: Up to €15,000 gross per month, including bonuses.
Possible Career Paths
After several years in this position, a Hotel Development Director can advance to:
- General Manager of a hotel group
- Director of International Expansion or Development
- Strategic Consultant or Hotel Investment Expert
- Creation and management of their own tourist real estate consulting firm

In France and internationally, the 50,000 Vatel alumni build exemplary, innovative, and exciting careers every day. They work in diverse sectors such as luxury hospitality, gourmet restaurants, event management, hotel marketing, luxury management, oenology, cruises, international tourism, and the wine & spirits industry.

jobs.title: Hotel General Manager
jobs.description:
Job Profiles
Hotel General Manager
The role of a hotel manager could be the perfect fit. The hotel manager is responsible for overseeing, organizing, and developing the activities of a hotel or franchised property.
Main Responsibilities
A hotel manager wears many hats and handles numerous responsibilities. He/she has to manage a team that deals with the following aspects:
- Defining the commercial offer: market analysis, setting rates, preparing the annual budget, investment decisions.
- Recruitment and team management: hiring, training, and motivating staff (reception, restaurant, housekeeping…).
- Organizing supplies: managing equipment, inventory, and logistics.
- Budget and partnerships management: accounting oversight, supplier selection, negotiation with local or cultural partners.
- Customer satisfaction and loyalty: supervising service quality, guest reception, and comfort.
- Marketing and communication: promoting the hotel internally and externally, attending trade shows, managing partnerships, digital marketing, and social media.
Skills and Personal Qualities
Technical and Managerial Skills:
A hotel manager functions as a true business leader, able to:
- Manage diverse activities coherently.
- Develop and implement an effective commercial strategy.
- Ensure and monitor the profitability of the property.
- Produce and utilize financial and economic analyses.
- Evaluate service-by-service performance and make necessary adjustments.
Soft Skills:
To succeed, a hotel manager should have:
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.
- Active listening abilities with colleagues, suppliers, and guests.
- A strong sense of service and customer satisfaction.
- Organization, rigor, and planning skills.
- Initiative and decision-making capacity.
- Flexibility and adaptability.
- Strong sense of responsibility.
- Ability to anticipate and manage emergencies.
Salary
Compensation varies depending on the size of the property and employment status (employee or independent):
- Average salary: over €45,000 gross per year.
- Additional benefits: performance bonuses, profit-sharing, and other incentives linked to hotel performance.
Education and Qualifications
- Bachelor of Management in Hospitality & Tourism
- MBA in Hotel & Tourism is often required for direct access to managerial positions.
Several years of experience in the hospitality sector are essential before leading a property.
Working Conditions
- Flexible and sometimes long hours.
- Full responsibility for the establishment.
- Constant interaction with guests, partners, and teams.
Career Progression
After gaining experience, a hotel manager can:
- Manage larger properties.
- Move into executive positions within a hotel group.
- Open or operate their own hotel.
- Specialize in emerging concepts (e.g., eco-lodges or sustainable hospitality).

In France and internationally, the 50,000 Vatel alumni build exemplary, innovative, and exciting careers every day. They work in diverse sectors such as luxury hospitality, gourmet restaurants, event management, hotel marketing, luxury management, oenology, cruises, international tourism, and the wine & spirits industry.

Job Profiles
Hotel General Manager
The role of a hotel manager could be the perfect fit. The hotel manager is responsible for overseeing, organizing, and developing the activities of a hotel or franchised property.
Main Responsibilities
A hotel manager wears many hats and handles numerous responsibilities. He/she has to manage a team that deals with the following aspects:
- Defining the commercial offer: market analysis, setting rates, preparing the annual budget, investment decisions.
- Recruitment and team management: hiring, training, and motivating staff (reception, restaurant, housekeeping…).
- Organizing supplies: managing equipment, inventory, and logistics.
- Budget and partnerships management: accounting oversight, supplier selection, negotiation with local or cultural partners.
- Customer satisfaction and loyalty: supervising service quality, guest reception, and comfort.
- Marketing and communication: promoting the hotel internally and externally, attending trade shows, managing partnerships, digital marketing, and social media.
Skills and Personal Qualities
Technical and Managerial Skills:
A hotel manager functions as a true business leader, able to:
- Manage diverse activities coherently.
- Develop and implement an effective commercial strategy.
- Ensure and monitor the profitability of the property.
- Produce and utilize financial and economic analyses.
- Evaluate service-by-service performance and make necessary adjustments.
Soft Skills:
To succeed, a hotel manager should have:
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.
- Active listening abilities with colleagues, suppliers, and guests.
- A strong sense of service and customer satisfaction.
- Organization, rigor, and planning skills.
- Initiative and decision-making capacity.
- Flexibility and adaptability.
- Strong sense of responsibility.
- Ability to anticipate and manage emergencies.
Salary
Compensation varies depending on the size of the property and employment status (employee or independent):

- Additional benefits: performance bonuses, profit-sharing, and other incentives linked to hotel performance.

jobs.title: Finance Director
jobs.description:
Job Profiles
Finance Director
In the hospitality and tourism sector, finance holds a strategic position. The Finance Director (or Chief Financial Officer - CFO) is responsible of their establishment's financial policy. This includes managing cash flow, planning budgets, handling taxation, analyzing performance, and managing risks.
Main Responsibilities
The Finance Director is a key player in hotel management. Their responsibilities revolve around several major areas:
- Cash and Financial Management: This involves tracking liquidity, working capital, and accounting indicators to guide the financial strategy.
- Budget Planning: They define short- and long-term financial objectives and develop budgets.
- Financial Analysis and Reporting: This includes collecting and presenting performance data and communicating results to shareholders and managers.
- Taxation and Regulation: They oversee tax and legal obligations and validate contracts and fiscal choices.
- Financial Risk Management: They identify and mitigate risks related to credit, exchange rates, liquidity, or contracts.
Skills and Personal Qualities
Technical Skills
- Strong knowledge of finance, taxation, management control, and commercial law.
- Mastery of financial information systems, accounting software, and management tools.
- Experience in banking relations, both national and international.
- A solid understanding of economics and financial markets.
- Fluent in written and spoken English, which is essential in the international sector.
Soft Skills
- Leadership and team management.
- Analytical and synthesis skills to interpret and utilize data.
- Meticulousness, a sense of organization, and foresight.
- Excellent interpersonal skills to convince partners, investors, and shareholders.
- Stress resilience and a high level of availability, often with frequent travel.
- Flexibility and responsiveness in a fast-paced environment.
Education and Degrees
A Bac +5 (Master's level) degree is recommended, with a specialization in finance, economics, accounting, or auditing. An MBA in International Hospitality is particularly well-suited for developing financial expertise applied specifically to the hotel and tourism sector. Significant experience in finance and/or hospitality is a major asset.
Working Conditions
- This is a position with significant strategic responsibility.
- Frequent travel is common, especially for CFOs of international hotel groups.
- Work hours are often long due to financial deadlines.
Salary
Compensation depends on the company's size and prestige, the country, and experience:
- Entry-level: Starting from €4,000 gross per month.
- Confirmed professional: Around €60,000 gross per year (the median salary in France).
- Senior Financial Director: Up to €15,000 gross per month in large international groups.
Career Progression
- Finance Director of a hotel group.
- General Manager of a hotel or hotel chain.
- The possibility of moving into strategic roles in other sectors (banking, consulting, multinational corporations).

In France and internationally, the 50,000 Vatel alumni build exemplary, innovative, and exciting careers every day. jobs.title: Revenue Manager
jobs.description:
Job Profiles
Revenue Manager
In the tourism, hospitality, or leisure industries, this role combines commercial strategy with market analysis. The Revenue Manager , also known as Yield Manager , optimizes an establishment's profitability through pricing strategies tailored to its business and market fluctuations. They use a blend of analytical, commercial, and digital skills to maximize revenue.
Main Responsibilities
The Revenue Manager's role is based on a detailed knowledge of the company, the market, and the customer base. Their main duties are:
- Continuous Market Analysis: This involves tracking the establishment's activity (bookings, cancellations, occupancy rates) and conducting competitive intelligence.
- Creating Forecasts and Budgets: They establish medium- and long-term calendars, and plan pricing policies and commercial actions to optimize business.
- Monitoring Commercial Activity: They analyze key indicators (bookings, revenue, available capacity) and report the results to management.
- Defining and Managing Pricing: They adjust prices based on demand and the market, establish new rate grids, and contribute to increasing revenue.
Skills
Technical and Analytical Skills:
- An analytical mind and the ability to interpret a wide range of indicators.
- Proficiency in IT tools and specialized revenue management software.
- A solid understanding of hospitality and tourism market trends.
Interpersonal and Communication Skills:
- Clear and persuasive communication to present analyses and recommendations.
- A team-oriented mindset and the ability to collaborate with other departments (sales, marketing, reception).
- A command of business English is essential for interacting with clients and partners.
Education
To enter this profession, an MBA in Hospitality and Tourism is recommended. This training allows you to:
- Master the fundamentals of revenue management and hotel distribution.
- Develop strong analytical and commercial skills.
- Learn to use digital tools and data to optimize pricing strategy.
Salary
The salary varies based on experience and the type of establishment:
- Entry-level: Between €32,000 and €40,000 gross per year.
- Senior-level: Around €60,000 gross per year.
Career Progression
After several years of experience, a Revenue Manager can advance to:
- Director of Revenue Management, overseeing multiple Revenue Managers.
- Director of Sales and Marketing, combining pricing and marketing strategy.
- Assistant General Manager or General Manager, thanks to their deep understanding of the company and the market.

Job Profiles
Revenue Manager
In the tourism, hospitality, or leisure industries, this role combines commercial strategy with market analysis. The Revenue Manager , also known as Yield Manager , optimizes an establishment's profitability through pricing strategies tailored to its business and market fluctuations. They use a blend of analytical, commercial, and digital skills to maximize revenue.
Main Responsibilities
The Revenue Manager's role is based on a detailed knowledge of the company, the market, and the customer base. Their main duties are:
- Continuous Market Analysis: This involves tracking the establishment's activity (bookings, cancellations, occupancy rates) and conducting competitive intelligence.
- Creating Forecasts and Budgets: They establish medium- and long-term calendars, and plan pricing policies and commercial actions to optimize business.
- Monitoring Commercial Activity: They analyze key indicators (bookings, revenue, available capacity) and report the results to management.
- Defining and Managing Pricing: They adjust prices based on demand and the market, establish new rate grids, and contribute to increasing revenue.
Skills
Technical and Analytical Skills:
- An analytical mind and the ability to interpret a wide range of indicators.
- Proficiency in IT tools and specialized revenue management software.
- A solid understanding of hospitality and tourism market trends.
Interpersonal and Communication Skills:
- Clear and persuasive communication to present analyses and recommendations.
- A team-oriented mindset and the ability to collaborate with other departments (sales, marketing, reception).
- A command of business English is essential for interacting with clients and partners.
Education
To enter this profession, an MBA in Hospitality and Tourism is recommended. This training allows you to:
- Master the fundamentals of revenue management and hotel distribution.
- Develop strong analytical and commercial skills.
- Learn to use digital tools and data to optimize pricing strategy.
Salary
The salary varies based on experience and the type of establishment:
- Entry-level: Between €32,000 and €40,000 gross per year.
- Senior-level: Around €60,000 gross per year.
Career Progression
After several years of experience, a Revenue Manager can advance to:
- Director of Revenue Management, overseeing multiple Revenue Managers.
- Director of Sales and Marketing, combining pricing and marketing strategy.
- Assistant General Manager or General Manager, thanks to their deep understanding of the company and the market.

In France and internationally, the 50,000 Vatel alumni build exemplary, innovative, and exciting careers every day. They work in diverse sectors such as luxury hospitality, gourmet restaurants, event management, hotel marketing, luxury management, oenology, cruises, international tourism, and the wine & spirits industry.

jobs.title: Event Project Manager / Events Manager
jobs.description:
Job Profiles
Event Project Manager / Events Manager
Do you have a strong sense of organization? Excellent communication skills? Creative flair? If you check all these boxes, you could become an Event Project Manager .
Event Project Manager
As a true conductor, you would organize and supervise a wide variety of events—such as trade shows, seminars, conferences, and awards ceremonies—on behalf of a company or for external clients. Your goal would be to create unifying experiences, strengthen cohesion, and contribute to the company's communication and brand strategy.
Main Responsibilities
The Event Project Manager designs, organizes, and supervises every step of a project:
- Planning: You'll analyze the project's feasibility, create the specifications, and define the key stages.
- Vendor Coordination: This involves selecting, negotiating with, and managing partners, such as caterers, decorators, and technical staff.
- Contingency Management: You'll anticipate risks and put backup plans in place.
- Operational Supervision: On the day of the event, you'll ensure everything runs smoothly and that the event is a success.
- Evaluation: You'll measure the event's impact and participant satisfaction, then handle the administrative closeout of the project.
Required Skills
Technical Skills
- Project Management: This includes planning, team coordination, and managing cross-functional services.
- Event Marketing and Communication: You need to understand the challenges and implement appropriate actions.
- Budget and Regulatory Management: You'll create and track budgets and ensure compliance with standards and procedures.
- Competitive Analysis: You'll study the market, perform benchmarking, and provide strategic recommendations.
- Commercial Negotiation: This includes writing proposals and responding to calls for tender.
Personal Qualities
- Creativity
- Organization and meticulousness
- Stress resilience
- Interpersonal and communication skills
- Agility and flexibility
- Business sense
Education and Degrees
- A Bachelor's degree in International Hospitality at Vatel (with a focus on communication, marketing, or events).
- An MBA in International Hospitality (with a focus on event engineering, management, finance, and communication).
Working Conditions
- Location: You can work for a company, an event agency, or as a freelancer.
- Hours: Work hours are often irregular and require availability in the evenings or on weekends.
- Travel: Frequent travel is common, depending on the nature of the events.
Salary
- Entry-level: Between €26,000 and €38,000 gross per year, with rapid progression based on experience.
- Bonuses: There is a possibility of bonuses tied to the success of events.
Career Progression
- Event Project Director after a few years of experience.
- Starting your own specialized agency to work independently.
Success Stories of Vatel Graduates
Vatel alumni have gone on to lead prestigious hotels, innovate in luxury hospitality, and develop unique tourism concepts, illustrating the opportunities this career path offers in France and internationally

descriptionByLocale.fr:
Job Profiles
Event Project Manager / Events Manager
Do you have a strong sense of organization? Excellent communication skills? Creative flair? If you check all these boxes, you could become an Event Project Manager .
Event Project Manager
As a true conductor, you would organize and supervise a wide variety of events—such as trade shows, seminars, conferences, and awards ceremonies—on behalf of a company or for external clients. Your goal would be to create unifying experiences, strengthen cohesion, and contribute to the company's communication and brand strategy.
Main Responsibilities
The Event Project Manager designs, organizes, and supervises every step of a project:
- Planning: You'll analyze the project's feasibility, create the specifications, and define the key stages.
- Vendor Coordination: This involves selecting, negotiating with, and managing partners, such as caterers, decorators, and technical staff.
- Contingency Management: You'll anticipate risks and put backup plans in place.
- Operational Supervision: On the day of the event, you'll ensure everything runs smoothly and that the event is a success.
- Evaluation: You'll measure the event's impact and participant satisfaction, then handle the administrative closeout of the project.
Required Skills
Technical Skills
- Project Management: This includes planning, team coordination, and managing cross-functional services.
- Event Marketing and Communication: You need to understand the challenges and implement appropriate actions.
- Budget and Regulatory Management: You'll create and track budgets and ensure compliance with standards and procedures.
- Competitive Analysis: You'll study the market, perform benchmarking, and provide strategic recommendations.
- Commercial Negotiation: This includes writing proposals and responding to calls for tender.
Personal Qualities
- Creativity
- Organization and meticulousness
- Stress resilience
- Interpersonal and communication skills
- Agility and flexibility
- Business sense
Education and Degrees
- A Bachelor's degree in International Hospitality at Vatel (with a focus on communication, marketing, or events).
- An MBA in International Hospitality (with a focus on event engineering, management, finance, and communication).
Working Conditions
- Location: You can work for a company, an event agency, or as a freelancer.
- Hours: Work hours are often irregular and require availability in the evenings or on weekends.
- Travel: Frequent travel is common, depending on the nature of the events.
Salary
- Entry-level: Between €26,000 and €38,000 gross per year, with rapid progression based on experience.
- Bonuses: There is a possibility of bonuses tied to the success of events.
Career Progression
- Event Project Director after a few years of experience.
- Starting your own specialized agency to work independently.

Vatel alumni have gone on to lead prestigious hotels, innovate in luxury hospitality, and develop unique tourism concepts, illustrating the opportunities this career path offers in France and internationally

jobs.title: Entrepreneur in Hospitality and Tourism
jobs.description:
Job Profiles
Entrepreneur in Hospitality and Tourism
Creating and managing your own hotel, restaurant, franchise, or leisure facility requires a strong entrepreneurial spirit. The entrepreneur in hospitality and tourism combines strategic vision, administrative management, and a sense of hospitality to build a profitable and sustainable business.
Main Responsibilities
The duties of an entrepreneur in the hospitality and tourism sector are numerous and varied:
- Design a business plan: Conduct market research, develop a strategic plan, and seek funding from banks or investors.
- Manage administration and finances: Choose a legal status, oversee accounting, manage cash flow, and recruit staff.
- Manage teams: Supervise various departments depending on the size of the business and ensure the quality of services.
- Define the commercial policy: Implement sales strategies, set pricing, establish a quality charter, and strictly comply with hygiene and safety standards.
- Listen to the clientele: Guarantee customer satisfaction, oversee the welcome, and improve the overall guest experience.
- Monitor revenue and profitability: Analyze results, optimize sales, and control costs.
Skills and Personal Qualities
Technical Skills
- Knowledge of administrative management, accounting, and taxation.
- Solid understanding of human resources management.
- Mastery of communication and marketing techniques to promote the business.
Soft Skills
- Leadership and a strong decision-making ability.
- Organization, meticulousness, and foresight.
- Adaptability to market fluctuations.
- A strong business acumen and excellent interpersonal skills to build customer loyalty.
- Resilience to the stress and pressure of running a business.
Education and Degrees
You'll generally need a Bac +3 to Bac +5 degree in hotel management, business, or entrepreneurship. The Vatel MBA is an excellent preparation, as it provides comprehensive expertise in hotel management, business strategy, and entrepreneurial project development.
Working Conditions
- A heavy workload, especially during the project launch phase.
- Multiple responsibilities (management, administration, strategy).
- Long and often unconventional hours, typical of the hotel and restaurant industry.
Salary
An entrepreneur's income depends directly on their business's profitability and revenue. In the launch phase, income can be modest or even nonexistent. As the business matures, earnings can become very high, depending on its size and location.
Career Progression
- Develop and manage multiple establishments.
- Create a group or a franchise.
- Diversify into other activities (sustainable tourism, innovative dining, related services).
Success Stories of Vatel Graduates
In France and internationally, the 50,000 Vatel alumni build exemplary, innovative, and exciting careers every day. They work in diverse sectors such as luxury hospitality, gourmet restaurants, event management, hotel marketing, luxury management, oenology, cruises, international tourism, and the wine & spirits industry.

jobs.title: Hotel Management Lecturer or Consultant
jobs.description:
Job Profiles
Hotel Management Lecturer or Consultant
A Hotel Management Lecturer shares his/her expertise with students and with professionals in continuing education. Based at a school specializing in hospitality, food service and tourism, he/she passes on both theory and hands-on know-how to shape the next generation of industry leaders.
Responsibilities
- Transmit knowledge: Design and lead classes on hotel management, property operations, business strategy, and best practices in the sector.
- Adapt educational content: Create training materials tailored to students and the needs of the hotel and restaurant market.
- Mentor learners: Supervise projects, advise students on their career choices, and help them get established in the industry.
- Stay up-to-date: Keep current with developments in the hotel market, consumer trends, and new management practices.
- Provide expert advice: Participate in seminars, conferences, or specialized modules based on your areas of expertise.
Skills and Qualities of a Hotel Management Lecturer or Consultant
- Industry expertise: Have a strong background in hospitality, catering, or tourism, with management responsibilities.
- Teaching abilities: Know how to explain, convey, and simplify complex concepts.
- Interpersonal and communication skills: Be able to capture an audience's attention and lead a lively and interactive class.
- Organization and rigor: Prepare your sessions, structure your content, and manage time effectively.
- Foreign language proficiency: English is often required, and sometimes other languages depending on the school or students.
- Digital tool usage: Be comfortable with e-learning, multimedia materials, and educational platforms.
Education and Career Path
There isn't one single path to becoming a hotel management speaker. The majority of lecturers are:
- Experienced professionals from the hotel or tourism sector (hotel directors, F&B managers, revenue managers, HR directors, etc.) who want to share their expertise.
- Holders of a master's degree ( MBA in hospitality at Vatel , master's in hospitality management, or business).
Some schools also prefer candidates with international experience.
Salary of a Hotel Management Lecturer or Consultant
- Part-time lecturer: Paid per course or conference, between €40 and €100 per hour depending on the institution.
- Full-time faculty member: Average annual salary between €35,000 and €50,000 gross, which varies with experience and status.
Possible Career Progression
- Become an Academic Director or Program Director at a hotel school.
- Transition into a career as a Training Consultant or Professional Coach .
- Specialize in academic research or take on a leadership role in higher education.
- Return to a senior management position in the hospitality industry, leveraging the expertise gained from teaching.
Success Stories of Vatel Graduates
In France and internationally, the 50,000 Vatel alumni build exemplary, innovative, and exciting careers every day. They work in diverse sectors such as luxury hospitality, gourmet restaurants, event management, hotel marketing, luxury management, oenology, cruises, international tourism, and the wine & spirits industry.

Job Profiles
Hotel Management Lecturer or Consultant
A Hotel Management Lecturer shares his/her expertise with students and with professionals in continuing education. Based at a school specializing in hospitality, food service and tourism, he/she passes on both theory and hands-on know-how to shape the next generation of industry leaders.
Responsibilities
- Transmit knowledge: Design and lead classes on hotel management, property operations, business strategy, and best practices in the sector.
- Adapt educational content: Create training materials tailored to students and the needs of the hotel and restaurant market.
- Mentor learners: Supervise projects, advise students on their career choices, and help them get established in the industry.
- Stay up-to-date: Keep current with developments in the hotel market, consumer trends, and new management practices.
- Provide expert advice: Participate in seminars, conferences, or specialized modules based on your areas of expertise.
Skills and Qualities of a Hotel Management Lecturer or Consultant
- Industry expertise: Have a strong background in hospitality, catering, or tourism, with management responsibilities.
- Teaching abilities: Know how to explain, convey, and simplify complex concepts.
- Interpersonal and communication skills: Be able to capture an audience's attention and lead a lively and interactive class.
- Organization and rigor: Prepare your sessions, structure your content, and manage time effectively.
- Foreign language proficiency: English is often required, and sometimes other languages depending on the school or students.
- Digital tool usage: Be comfortable with e-learning, multimedia materials, and educational platforms.
Education and Career Path
There isn't one single path to becoming a hotel management speaker. The majority of lecturers are:
- Experienced professionals from the hotel or tourism sector (hotel directors, F&B managers, revenue managers, HR directors, etc.) who want to share their expertise.
- Holders of a master's degree ( MBA in hospitality at Vatel , master's in hospitality management, or business).
Some schools also prefer candidates with international experience.
Salary of a Hotel Management Lecturer or Consultant
- Part-time lecturer: Paid per course or conference, between €40 and €100 per hour depending on the institution.
- Full-time faculty member: Average annual salary between €35,000 and €50,000 gross, which varies with experience and status.
Possible Career Progression
- Become an Academic Director or Program Director at a hotel school.
- Transition into a career as a Training Consultant or Professional Coach .
- Specialize in academic research or take on a leadership role in higher education.
- Return to a senior management position in the hospitality industry, leveraging the expertise gained from teaching.
Success Stories of Vatel Graduates
In France and internationally, the 50,000 Vatel alumni build exemplary, innovative, and exciting careers every day. They work in diverse sectors such as luxury hospitality, gourmet restaurants, event management, hotel marketing, luxury management, oenology, cruises, international tourism, and the wine & spirits industry.

jobs.title: Sales Manager
jobs.description:
Job Profiles
Sales Manager
If you're passionate about hospitality or tourism, the Sales Manager is a key figure in driving growth.
Their role is to define and implement a commercial strategy that increases revenue and builds customer loyalty for an establishment. As a highly sought-after and crucial position, it offers excellent career and salary prospects.
Main Responsibilities
As a Sales Manager, your duties revolve around four main areas:
- Define and Achieve Sales Targets: You'll create a commercial action plan and a sales optimization strategy to meet the goals set by management.
- Implement the Commercial Strategy: This involves applying the company's marketing plan, analyzing performance, evaluating sales, and reporting on the results.
- Recruit and Lead a Team: You'll recruit, train, and manage the sales team. You'll also organize meetings and set individual and collective goals.
- Develop and Retain the Client Portfolio: You'll deploy prospecting and customer retention actions through digital marketing (social media, emailing, blogs) and direct field contact.
Technical Skills
The role of a Sales Manager requires a solid set of skills:
- Commercial and Digital Techniques: You need to master the fundamentals of sales, prospecting, and closing deals. Knowledge of digital marketing and communication is also essential.
- Management and Leadership: The ability to recruit, train, and unite a team is crucial. You also need an entrepreneurial vision and a strong business sense.
- Analysis and Management: You'll be responsible for monitoring budgets, using reporting tools, and analyzing results to optimize the commercial strategy.
- Foreign Languages: Business English is a must-have in hospitality and tourism, and a third language is a significant advantage.
Soft Skills
To excel as a Sales Manager, certain human qualities are essential:
- A knack for summarizing and synthesizing information.
- Excellent written and interpersonal communication skills.
- Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
- The ability to listen and a sense of diplomacy.
- Charisma and natural leadership.
Education
A degree is essential for this high-responsibility position. A Vatel MBA , or an MBA in commerce, marketing, or hospitality/tourism (equivalent to a Bachelor's + 4 or 5 years of study), is highly recommended. Specialized training in e-marketing and hotel management is also valuable. International MBAs are particularly valued for those who want to work in multicultural environments.
Salary
A Sales Manager on a permanent contract can expect to earn between €4,500 and €5,800 gross per month. This salary can vary based on sales bonuses, the size of the company, level of experience, and the country where you work.
Career Progression
The Sales Manager role offers numerous career paths:
- International Sales Manager: Managing international markets.
- Marketing Director: Overseeing commercial and communication strategies.
- Branch Director: Managing all aspects of a business unit.
- Independent Consultant: Assisting companies with their commercial development.
Success Stories of Vatel Graduates
In France and internationally, the 50,000 Vatel alumni build exemplary, innovative, and exciting careers every day. They work in diverse sectors such as luxury hospitality, gourmet restaurants, event management, hotel marketing, luxury management, oenology, cruises, international tourism, and the wine & spirits industry.

Their role is to define and implement a commercial strategy that increases revenue and builds customer loyalty for an establishment. As a highly sought-after and crucial position, it offers excellent career and salary prospects.
Main Responsibilities
As a Sales Manager, your duties revolve around four main areas:
- Define and Achieve Sales Targets: You'll create a commercial action plan and a sales optimization strategy to meet the goals set by management.
- Implement the Commercial Strategy: This involves applying the company's marketing plan, analyzing performance, evaluating sales, and reporting on the results.
- Recruit and Lead a Team: You'll recruit, train, and manage the sales team. You'll also organize meetings and set individual and collective goals.
- Develop and Retain the Client Portfolio: You'll deploy prospecting and customer retention actions through digital marketing (social media, emailing, blogs) and direct field contact.
Technical Skills
The role of a Sales Manager requires a solid set of skills:
- Commercial and Digital Techniques: You need to master the fundamentals of sales, prospecting, and closing deals. Knowledge of digital marketing and communication is also essential.
- Management and Leadership: The ability to recruit, train, and unite a team is crucial. You also need an entrepreneurial vision and a strong business sense.
- Analysis and Management: You'll be responsible for monitoring budgets, using reporting tools, and analyzing results to optimize the commercial strategy.
- Foreign Languages: Business English is a must-have in hospitality and tourism, and a third language is a significant advantage.
Soft Skills
To excel as a Sales Manager, certain human qualities are essential:
- A knack for summarizing and synthesizing information.
- Excellent written and interpersonal communication skills.
- Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
- The ability to listen and a sense of diplomacy.
- Charisma and natural leadership.
Education
A degree is essential for this high-responsibility position. A Vatel MBA , or an MBA in commerce, marketing, or hospitality/tourism (equivalent to a Bachelor's + 4 or 5 years of study), is highly recommended. Specialized training in e-marketing and hotel management is also valuable. International MBAs are particularly valued for those who want to work in multicultural environments.
Salary
A Sales Manager on a permanent contract can expect to earn between €4,500 and €5,800 gross per month. This salary can vary based on sales bonuses, the size of the company, level of experience, and the country where you work.
Career Progression
The Sales Manager role offers numerous career paths:
- International Sales Manager: Managing international markets.
- Marketing Director: Overseeing commercial and communication strategies.
- Branch Director: Managing all aspects of a business unit.
- Independent Consultant: Assisting companies with their commercial development.
Success Stories of Vatel Graduates
In France and internationally, the 50,000 Vatel alumni build exemplary, innovative, and exciting careers every day. They work in diverse sectors such as luxury hospitality, gourmet restaurants, event management, hotel marketing, luxury management, oenology, cruises, international tourism, and the wine & spirits industry.

jobs.title: Marketing Manager
jobs.description:
Job Profiles
Marketing Manager
In the hospitality, tourism, and leisure industries, commercial success hinges on an effective marketing strategy. The Marketing Manager defines this strategy and coordinates its implementation to increase the visibility, brand awareness, and revenue of the establishment.
Main Responsibilities
The role of a Marketing Manager is built on a deep understanding of the company, the market, and the customers. Their main responsibilities are:
- Define the Marketing Strategy and Commercial Objectives: This includes launching new services, entering new markets, and developing the business.
- Study the Market and Analyze the Competition: They identify customer needs, market trends, and constraints.
- Enhance Brand Awareness and Company Communication: They create a multi-channel communication plan (digital, social media, traditional media, events).
- Coordinate Teams and Partners: They manage marketing teams, oversee projects, and collaborate with external public, private, or institutional partners.
- Measure the Effectiveness of Actions: This involves analyzing marketing performance, tracking key indicators, and making strategic adjustments.
Required Skills
Technical Skills
- Mastery of both digital and traditional marketing.
- Market analysis and competitive intelligence.
- Project management and strategic planning.
- Communication and negotiation with internal and external partners.
Soft Skills
- Curiosity and strong observation skills.
- Team spirit and leadership.
- Autonomy, creativity, and adaptability.
- The ability to solve complex problems and make decisions.
Education
A Marketing Manager typically needs a Bac +5 level of education (equivalent to a Master's degree). Possible paths include:
- A Bachelor's degree in International Hospitality (with a focus on communication, marketing, or events).
- An MBA in International Hospitality (focusing on event engineering, management, finance, and communication).
- A Bachelor's degree followed by an MBA or a specialized Master's in marketing, commerce, or communication.
- Business schools or specialized institutes in marketing and management.
- Complementary training in data and customer behavior analysis to refine marketing strategies.
Companies That Hire
Marketing Manager profiles are highly sought after in the hospitality and tourism sectors, including:
- International and national hotel chains.
- Hotels, luxury hotels, and resorts.
- Travel agencies and tour operators.
- Leisure companies, cafes-hotels-restaurants (CHRs), and event organizations.
Salary
The salary varies based on the company size, experience, and location:
- Junior Marketing Manager: Approximately €3,000 gross per month.
- Median Salary: €43,000 gross per year.
- Experienced Manager in a Large Group: Between €10,000 and €13,000 gross per month.
Career Progression
The Marketing Manager position is a stepping stone to higher-level responsibilities:
- Marketing Director
- Marketing or Commercial Strategy Consultant
- Marketing Manager for an International or Multi-site Group

Vatel alumni have gone on to lead prestigious hotels, innovate in luxury hospitality, and develop unique tourism concepts, illustrating the opportunities this career path offers in France and internationally.

jobs.title: Manager in the Luxury Sector
jobs.description:
Job Profiles
Manager in the Luxury Sector
Whether in prestige hospitality, haute couture, or jewelry , the Manager in the Luxury Sector is an ambassador of excellence . Their role is to satisfy a demanding, high-end clientele by ensuring that every service is flawless and in line with the brand image they represent.
Responsibilities
The luxury sector is divided into two categories:
- Material Luxury (fashion, jewelry, leather goods, etc.)
- Experiential Luxury (tourism, hospitality, gastronomy), which represents 64% of the global market.
In this rapidly growing sector, the specialized Luxury Manager fulfills various missions:
- Maintain Brand Reputation: Define and implement a commercial policy consistent with the brand's image, recruit and supervise rare talents, and attract new clients.
- Cultivate Loyalty in High-End Clientele: Create a privileged relationship with the most important clients, devise personalized gestures, and guarantee a unique experience.
- Promote the Brand's History and Identity: Transmit the values, tell the story, and highlight the brand's distinguishing assets.
- Participate in the Communication Plan: Collaborate with marketing, suggest improvements, and adapt offerings to the evolving luxury market.
Did You Know?
The luxury industry is prosperous: in 2021, the global high-end luxury market represented nearly 283 billion euros (source: Les Échos).
Required Skills and Qualities
Technical Skills
- Cultural Knowledge: Understanding the customs, conventions, and expectations of an international clientele.
- Market Research Methods: Analyzing trends and purchasing behaviors to define an appropriate strategy.
- Pricing Management Techniques: Mastery of yield management (flexible pricing), particularly in hospitality.
- Luxury Codes: Adherence to the aesthetic, protocol, and behavioral standards specific to the sector.
- Foreign Languages: Fluent English is essential; Chinese or Russian are highly valued.
- Human Resources Management: Supervising and motivating teams (department heads, reception, sales, etc.).
Personal Qualities (Soft Skills)
- Rigor and attention to detail.
- Aesthetic sense and refinement.
- Adaptability and creativity.
- Excellent presentation and relational ease (interpersonal skills).
- Acute sense of service and prestige.
Education and Qualifications
To meet the sector's expectations, recruiters prioritize specialized training:
- Bachelor & MBA in Hotel Management, Business, or Luxury Management.
- Specialized MBAs (e.g., MBA in International Hospitality ) effectively prepare candidates for management positions in luxury by developing expertise in management, marketing, and high-end service.
Working Conditions
- Prestigious but highly demanding environment.
- Extended hours, often evenings or weekends.
- High international mobility depending on the position and the brand/house.
Salary
Compensation varies according to the sector, country, and level of responsibility:
- Luxury Boutique Manager: Between €3,100 and €4,100 gross/month.
- Luxury Hotel Director: Between €5,000 and €8,000 gross/month, excluding bonuses and profit-sharing linked to revenue.
Career Progression
A manager specializing in luxury can progress toward:
- General management positions in hospitality, fashion, or jewelry.
- Managing multiple establishments or boutiques.
- Strategic roles (Brand Manager, Marketing Director, Commercial Director).
With experience, they can also move into luxury strategy consulting or entrepreneurship .

descriptionByLocale.en:
Job Profiles
Manager in the Luxury Sector
Whether in prestige hospitality, haute couture, or jewelry , the Manager in the Luxury Sector is an ambassador of excellence . Their role is to satisfy a demanding, high-end clientele by ensuring that every service is flawless and in line with the brand image they represent.
Responsibilities
The luxury sector is divided into two categories:
- Material Luxury (fashion, jewelry, leather goods, etc.)
- Experiential Luxury (tourism, hospitality, gastronomy), which represents 64% of the global market.
In this rapidly growing sector, the specialized Luxury Manager fulfills various missions:
- Maintain Brand Reputation: Define and implement a commercial policy consistent with the brand's image, recruit and supervise rare talents, and attract new clients.
- Cultivate Loyalty in High-End Clientele: Create a privileged relationship with the most important clients, devise personalized gestures, and guarantee a unique experience.
- Promote the Brand's History and Identity: Transmit the values, tell the story, and highlight the brand's distinguishing assets.
- Participate in the Communication Plan: Collaborate with marketing, suggest improvements, and adapt offerings to the evolving luxury market.
Did You Know?
The luxury industry is prosperous: in 2021, the global high-end luxury market represented nearly 283 billion euros (source: Les Échos).
Required Skills and Qualities
Technical Skills
- Cultural Knowledge: Understanding the customs, conventions, and expectations of an international clientele.
- Market Research Methods: Analyzing trends and purchasing behaviors to define an appropriate strategy.
- Pricing Management Techniques: Mastery of yield management (flexible pricing), particularly in hospitality.
- Luxury Codes: Adherence to the aesthetic, protocol, and behavioral standards specific to the sector.
- Foreign Languages: Fluent English is essential; Chinese or Russian are highly valued.
- Human Resources Management: Supervising and motivating teams (department heads, reception, sales, etc.).
Personal Qualities (Soft Skills)
- Rigor and attention to detail.
- Aesthetic sense and refinement.
- Adaptability and creativity.
- Excellent presentation and relational ease (interpersonal skills).
- Acute sense of service and prestige.
Education and Qualifications
To meet the sector's expectations, recruiters prioritize specialized training:
- Bachelor & MBA in Hotel Management, Business, or Luxury Management.
- Specialized MBAs (e.g., MBA in International Hospitality ) effectively prepare candidates for management positions in luxury by developing expertise in management, marketing, and high-end service.
Working Conditions
- Prestigious but highly demanding environment.
- Extended hours, often evenings or weekends.
- High international mobility depending on the position and the brand/house.
Salary
Compensation varies according to the sector, country, and level of responsibility:
- Luxury Boutique Manager: Between €3,100 and €4,100 gross/month.
- Luxury Hotel Director: Between €5,000 and €8,000 gross/month, excluding bonuses and profit-sharing linked to revenue.
Career Progression
A manager specializing in luxury can progress toward:
- General management positions in hospitality, fashion, or jewelry.
- Managing multiple establishments or boutiques.
- Strategic roles (Brand Manager, Marketing Director, Commercial Director).
With experience, they can also move into luxury strategy consulting or entrepreneurship .
Success Stories of Vatel Graduates
In France and internationally, the 50,000 Vatel alumni build exemplary, innovative, and exciting careers every day. They work in diverse sectors such as luxury hospitality, gourmet restaurants, event management, hotel marketing, luxury management, oenology, cruises, international tourism, and the wine & spirits industry.
