jobs.description:
Job Profiles
Tourism and Hospitality Client Manager – Banking and Finance
Client Manager specializing in the tourism and hospitality industry is a relationship management professional who works within a bank.
Client Manager specializing in the tourism and hospitality industry is a relationship management professional who works within a bank. He/she supports hotels, travel agencies, tour operators, and other tourism businesses with account management, project financing, and cash flow optimization.
He/she acts as a dedicated point of contact, combining financial expertise with an in-depth understanding of the tourism industry.
Key 
• Responsibilities
The role of a Client Manager specializing in tourism and hospitality industry is to develop and retain a portfolio of professional clients within the tourism industry. Their main responsibilities include:
Client account management and monitoring: Following up on financial transactions, analyzing client needs and profitability, and providing personalized advice to optimize cash flow and investments.
Business development: Prospecting for new clients and creating financial solutions tailored to the industry's specific needs, such as loans, leasing, insurance, and financing for hotel or tourism projects.
Project support: Advising on financing solutions for the construction, renovation, or expansion of hotels and tourism facilities.
Client relations and retention : Maintaining regular contact with clients, monitoring their performance, anticipating their needs, and proposing custom solutions.
Required Skills
To succeed in this position, several skills are essential:
Financial and accounting skills: Expertise in financial analysis, banking products, and financing solutions.
Knowledge of the tourism/hospitality sector: Understanding the economic challenges, operational specifics, and business cycles of the industry.
Communication and client relations: The ability to negotiate, advise, and retain clients.
Organization and rigor: The capacity to manage multiple files simultaneously and adhere to banking procedures.
Proficiency in English and other foreign languages: Essential for dealing with international clients.
Education
A bachelor's or master's degree is generally required, with a specialization in banking, finance, management, or business. A background in hospitality and tourism ( MBA or Bachelor at Vatel) supplemented by financial training can also lead to this role. Experience in the tourism or hotel sector is highly valued.
Salary
The average salary for a Client Manager specializing in tourism and hospitality ranges from €30,000 to €45,000 gross per year at the beginning of their career. With experience and depending on the size of the bank or the complexity of their portfolio, it can reach €60,000 or more.
Career Progression
After several years of experience, a Client Manager can advance to:
Senior Professional Client Portfolio Manager
Bank Branch Manager specializing in tourism and hospitality
Corporate or Professional Market Relations Manager
Hotel and Tourism Financing Consultant

Job Profiles
Tourism and Hospitality Client Manager – Banking and Finance
Client Manager specializing in the tourism and hospitality industry is a relationship management professional who works within a bank.
Client Manager specializing in the tourism and hospitality industry is a relationship management professional who works within a bank. He/she supports hotels, travel agencies, tour operators, and other tourism businesses with account management, project financing, and cash flow optimization.
He/she acts as a dedicated point of contact, combining financial expertise with an in-depth understanding of the tourism industry.
Key 
• Responsibilities
The role of a Client Manager specializing in tourism and hospitality industry is to develop and retain a portfolio of professional clients within the tourism industry. Their main responsibilities include:
Client account management and monitoring: Following up on financial transactions, analyzing client needs and profitability, and providing personalized advice to optimize cash flow and investments.
Business development: Prospecting for new clients and creating financial solutions tailored to the industry's specific needs, such as loans, leasing, insurance, and financing for hotel or tourism projects.
Project support: Advising on financing solutions for the construction, renovation, or expansion of hotels and tourism facilities.
Client relations and retention : Maintaining regular contact with clients, monitoring their performance, anticipating their needs, and proposing custom solutions.
Required Skills
To succeed in this position, several skills are essential:
Financial and accounting skills: Expertise in financial analysis, banking products, and financing solutions.
Knowledge of the tourism/hospitality sector: Understanding the economic challenges, operational specifics, and business cycles of the industry.
Communication and client relations: The ability to negotiate, advise, and retain clients.
Organization and rigor: The capacity to manage multiple files simultaneously and adhere to banking procedures.
Proficiency in English and other foreign languages: Essential for dealing with international clients.
Education
A bachelor's or master's degree is generally required, with a specialization in banking, finance, management, or business. A background in hospitality and tourism ( MBA or Bachelor at Vatel) supplemented by financial training can also lead to this role. Experience in the tourism or hotel sector is highly valued.
Salary
The average salary for a Client Manager specializing in tourism and hospitality ranges from €30,000 to €45,000 gross per year at the beginning of their career. With experience and depending on the size of the bank or the complexity of their portfolio, it can reach €60,000 or more.
Career Progression
After several years of experience, a Client Manager can advance to:
Senior Professional Client Portfolio Manager
Bank Branch Manager specializing in tourism and hospitality
Corporate or Professional Market Relations Manager
Hotel and Tourism Financing Consultant

jobs.title: Hotel Auditor
jobs.description:
Job Profiles
Hotel Auditor
The Hotel Auditor is a professional specialized in evaluating the performance, compliance, and profitability of a hotel or tourist establishment. His/her role is to analyze management practices, service quality, regulatory compliance, and profitability in order to propose strategic recommendations . As a true expert in control and consulting, he/she assists hotels, resorts, and hotel chains in optimizing their operations and competitiveness.
Responsibilities
- Evaluate financial and operational management: Control budgets, costs, billing, and profit margins.
- Analyze compliance and service quality: Verify adherence to hygiene, safety, and quality standards (ISO, hotel labels, brand standards).
- Observe and audit processes: Analyze the work organization across various departments (accommodation, catering, front office, housekeeping, F&B).
- Measure client satisfaction: Through surveys, mystery audits, and monitoring online reviews.
- Formulate strategic recommendations: Suggest areas for improvement to optimize performance, reduce costs, or increase client satisfaction.
- Support management: Provide an external and objective perspective to guide strategic decisions.
Required Skills
- Solid knowledge of hotel management and financial analysis.
- Mastery of quality, safety, and hotel regulatory standards.
- Capacity for observation, analysis, and synthesis.
- Communication skills to present results and convince management.
- A sense of teaching (pedagogy) and guidance in change management.
- Good command of IT tools (reporting, ERP, hotel management software).
- Fluency in foreign languages (English in particular) is an asset for auditing international establishments.
Education to Become a Hotel Auditor
A degree level of Bac+3 to Bac+5 (Bachelor's to Master's equivalent) is generally required:
- Bachelor's in Hotel Management , Management, Audit, or Finance.
- MBA specialized in hospitality management or in audit and management control.
- Prior experience in the hotel industry (management, revenue management, management control, quality) is highly valued.
Specific certifications in quality auditing or internal control may complement the professional background.
Salary of a Hotel Auditor
- Entry-level: Between €2,800 and €3,500 gross per month.
- Confirmed Profile (Experienced): Between €3,500 and €5,000 gross per month.
- Senior or Independent: Up to €6,000 or more, depending on the size and reputation of the audited establishments.
Career Progression
After a few years, the Hotel Auditor can progress to roles such as:
- Quality Director in a hotel chain.
- Management Controller specializing in the hotel sector.
- Independent Consultant in the hotel and tourism industry.
- Hotel Director or Department Head (Accommodation, Catering, F&B) with reinforced expertise in operational steering.

Head of Promotion and Distribution in the Agri-Food Industry
Do you want to combine commercial strategy with operational management in the agri-food sector? The role of Head of Promotion and Distribution offers you this opportunity. At the crossroads of marketing, logistics, and customer relations, this role plays a key part in developing sales and optimizing product presence in the market.
Main Responsibilities
